title: The Confession of the Fens
premise: Insurance investigator Bram Reyes, whose photographic memory has made her the quiet keeper of the fen town of Marlowe Dike's secrets, is handed a cold case: the disappearance of schoolteacher Elowen Marsh, twelve years gone. When Bram discovers Elowen's recovered diary contains entries dated after her vanishing, she realizes someone kept writing in it—and that the diary doubles as a coded ledger recording the town's complicity in a drowning everyone agreed to forget. As the statute of limitations closes in, Bram must choose between exposing the found family that sheltered her and honoring the woman who never got to belong. In the end, she decodes the ledger, confronts the beloved innkeeper who orchestrated the cover-up to protect his own daughter, and chooses truth over silence—releasing the confession publicly while giving the daughter, now grown, the chance to finally come home.
about_author: Coral Lockridge grew up on the edge of the East Anglian fens, where winter fog could swallow a lane whole and every village kept one story no one told. A former archivist, she writes mysteries about the things small towns bury and the people who dig them up.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Bram Reyes, POV. Opening with Bram cataloguing claims in her meticulous mental archive, she's assigned the dormant Elowen Marsh file as its statute nears expiry. Reading Elowen's returned diary, she freezes: entries continue three days past the disappearance date. The emotional beat is unease—the first crack in the ordered world Bram built to stay invisible.

chapters.title: Ink After the Water
chapters.summary: Bram, POV, with flashbacks from Elowen's diary entries. Bram cross-references dates against town records and finds the post-disappearance entries encode sums of money—a ledger. Her questions unsettle the innkeeper, Aldous Crane, who raised her after her mother left. Rising tension: someone ransacks her office, and Bram realizes the diary's final entry names 'the girl who remembers.'

chapters.title: What the Fen Kept
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Decoding the cipher hidden in hymn numbers, Bram reconstructs the night Elowen drowned rescuing Aldous's teenage daughter Maren from the flooded drain—and how witnesses were paid to misremember. Climax: Bram confronts Aldous at the dike; he confesses, begging her to protect Maren as Elowen once did. Duty versus love tears at her.

chapters.title: The Statute of Belonging
chapters.summary: Bram, POV, closing with Maren's voice. Bram files the true confession before midnight, ending the cover-up but shielding Maren from prosecution as a child. Resolution: the town reels, yet begins to speak honestly; Maren returns home, and Bram—no longer invisible—is claimed by the family she chose. Final beat: she adds her own name to the ledger, freely given.
